Desk rules for floor markings
New staff will learn how the first steps go

This page explains how the floor markings guide movement at the Companion Animal Travel Desk and why careful use of them matters. Markings keep staff, travelers, and pets moving in an orderly way, and they reduce confusion at check-in, handoff, and recovery points. Follow the markings as fixed reference points, not as decoration or suggestion.

When you approach a marked area, pause long enough to read the flow of the space. Keep carriers aligned with the lane and leave the walk path clear for other travelers. Speak in calm, short statements so the traveler knows where to stand and where to wait. If a pet seems unsettled, keep your own pace steady and alert the senior coordinator before the situation spreads across the desk area.

Use the markings together with the kennel and cabin checks. One part of the job is confirming that the pet and carrier match the record and are placed in the right zone. <<FACT F067>> If a record note seems incomplete, stop the handoff and seek review before the carrier moves forward.

A second duty is guiding travelers to the correct pet cabin process for the aircraft. <<FACT F031>> Keep the explanation brief and respectful, and make sure the traveler understands that the cabin team will monitor the animal during flight.

For larger animals, the markings also help with safe lifting and staging. <<FACT F063>> Do not rush the transfer, and use approved help when the carrier is awkward or the pet is restless.

Remember to follow the markings, keep communication clear, and protect both the traveler and the animal at every step.
